---
title: "What should I set up when candidature begins?"
---

**Pause point:** Before beginning substantive research work.

**Prevents:** Starting without clear supervision, required access, a recoverable working system or awareness of local obligations.

**Use:** Read-do.

## Critical checks

- [ ] I have confirmed my official start date, enrolment status and next formal milestone in the institution's current system.
- [ ] I know who is formally on my supervisory team and have a first meeting booked.
- [ ] We have discussed responsibilities, contact expectations, feedback, meeting records and how decisions will be documented.
- [ ] I have identified required induction, research-integrity, safety, methods, ethics, data and professional-development training.
- [ ] I have an approved location for research files plus a separate action register and decision log.
- [ ] I can access the systems, rooms, software, equipment, data or services needed for the first phase.
- [ ] I know where to seek local help for candidature, wellbeing, integrity, ethics, data, safety and supervision concerns.
- [ ] I have agreed what must be achieved before the first 90-day review and what evidence will show it is done.

## Stop condition

Do not begin participant contact, data collection, access to restricted data, or hazardous work until the required approvals, training and supervision are in place.

## Evidence to retain

Keep the enrolment or milestone confirmation, induction record, supervision notes, training record, access confirmations, first action register and first decision-log entry.

## Scenario test

**Situation:** A newly enrolled student can access email and the library but has not confirmed the supervisory team, approved storage or safety training. They want to begin collecting pilot data.

**Result:** The student needs to confirm supervision, establish approved storage and complete the required approvals and training before collecting pilot data. Orientation searching and reversible planning may continue.
